primitives.meaning: a recorded failure: a service failure, a failed fulfilment, a confirmed disruption, a failed critical action, or severe support dissatisfaction
entryFilters: an authoritative record of a negative experience or service failure attributable to this person and an experience entity
no other recovery process is already handling the same failure
the underlying issue is resolved - nothing is said about a failure that is still ongoing

primitives.does: Establish what failed, what it cost the customer, whether it has been resolved, whether they are still affected, and whether some other process is already handling it

primitives.asks: Is another recovery process already handling this failure?

branches.label: Already handled
branches.test: an open case, an assigned owner or another recovery journey covers the same incident

primitives.state: deferred to the process already handling it
primitives.reEntry: if that process closes with the customer still affected, this re-opens - two apologies from two systems is worse than one, because it proves neither knew about the other

primitives.asks: Is the underlying issue still unresolved?

branches.label: Resolved
branches.test: the failure is over and the customer is no longer affected

primitives.on: a failure that is still ongoing
carries: what failed and who is affected
the fact that no recovery message has been sent yet
suppresses: apology and compensation messaging until the thing being apologised for has stopped happening

primitives.asks: Is a recovery communication actually useful here?

branches.label: Useful
branches.test: the customer noticed, or would want to know it was handled

branches.label: Not useful
branches.test: the failure was resolved before it reached them - raising it now creates the concern it would be apologising for

primitives.reEntry: a recurrence, or any sign they did notice, re-opens this

primitives.asks: Does policy and the actual impact support compensation?

branches.label: Owed
branches.test: the impact and the policy both support a remedy

branches.label: Not owed
branches.test: the failure was real but no remedy is justified - which is most failures

primitives.on: a remedy that policy and impact both support
carries: the failure and its assessed impact
what has already been said to the customer

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the acknowledgement should be something the person can keep - what failed, what was done, what prevents it - which is the default
the failure happened inside the app, the person is active there, and the acknowledgement is short

primitives.purpose: Say what failed, what was done about it, and what stops it happening again. No discount standing in for an explanation.
primitives.brief: Say what failed, what was done about it, and what stops it happening again. No discount standing in for an explanation - a remedy offered instead of an account of what went wrong reads as buying silence
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.reEntry: a recurrence changes the assessment, and repetition is itself part of the impact
